marks.gloss_en: a vine branch that is tied to a pitcher -- one may fill with it on Shabbat
a window shutter -- R' Eliezer: when it is tied and hanging, one may shutter with it
מאן דאמר גשוש -- כל שכן סואר: on the view that Rabbi's case was a ship's sounding pole (which one is particular about), all the more so a stack of beams
R' Yosei b. Shaul: it was a stack of beams
ואזדו לטעמייהו -- R' Ami, who transmitted 'it became a base', has Rabbi require arranging the stones
ואזדו לטעמייהו -- R' Asi, who transmitted 'it became a cover', has Rabbi require only rubbing the stones
Rabbi once came upon a course of stones and told his students: go and think [of them], so that we may sit on them tomorrow -- and Rabbi did not require them to do an action
מותבינן אשמעתין: האבן שבקירויה אם ממלאין בה ואינה נופלת ממלאין בה -- a stone placed for use is not a forbidden thing on which [the vessel] is a base
ולא היא -- התם כיון דהדקה שוייה דופן: there, since he pressed it in, he made it a wall [of the gourd]
ומותבינן אשמעתין: ואם לאו אין ממלאין בה -- a stone merely placed does not become part of the vessel
ולא היא -- התם כיון דלא הדקה בטולי בטלה: there, since he did not press it in, he nullified it [as part of the gourd]
a stone on the mouth of a barrel -- one tilts [the barrel] on its side and [the stone] falls
one master holds: an action is required [to make a set-aside object fit for use]
R' Yochanan: Rabbi required them to do an action
the mishna's clause on a window shutter (cited by its opening words)
קשורה -- אין, לא קשורה -- לא: from the mishna's 'tied' it follows that an untied branch is not permitted
the mishna: a vine branch that is tied [-- one may draw water with it on Shabbat]
דתניא: ... רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר: אין צריך לקשור -- RSBG requires no tying, while the mishna permits only a tied branch
palm branches cut for wood, about which he reconsidered [to use them] for sitting: he must tie [them]
אי הכי, קא משתמש במחובר לקרקע -- if so, he is making use of something attached to the ground!
למטה משלשה -- [the branch is attached] below three [handbreadths]
[the mishna holds] even if you say it is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's
the Sages: either way one may shutter [the window] with it
